title: ACPAcceptanceReport
description: The result of one run of the portable acceptance suite against one target. A SHARED format: the certification matrix, the support-status table and any release gate read this file rather than the suite's console output, so a field added here is a field consumers may rely on. The load-bearing rule is not structural and cannot be expressed in JSON Schema: supportClaim.mvpEligible is true only when every id in suite.mandatoryForMvp appears in scenarios with state 'pass'. skip and unknown are not passes. See acp_acceptance/report.py and tests/test_packaging_acceptance.py, which is where that rule is enforced and tested.

apiVersion.description: Contract version. A breaking change gets a new version rather than a redefined field, so an archived report keeps meaning what it meant when it was written.

synthetic.description: True whenever the run did not touch a real target — a --self-test run against the fake backend, or any other simulated execution. REQUIRED, so a report can never read as real acceptance evidence because a producer omitted the field, and supportClaim.mvpEligible/supportedEligible are forced false while it is true. Ten scenarios passing against a fake backend establishes that the suite works and nothing whatsoever about any target; PRD S7 requires a target to pass the acceptance, upgrade, restore and recovery gates before it is called supported.

durationSeconds.description: Wall-clock duration of the whole run. Present alongside the per-scenario timings because the difference between them is the suite's own overhead, and a certification run that spends most of its time in the harness is a finding of its own.

target.description: What the suite ran against. Deliberately five fields and no more: this block is an ALLOW-LIST built by Target.as_report_block(), not a serialisation of the descriptor, so that a kubeconfig context or a bearer token cannot arrive here by being added to the descriptor later.

name.description: The operator's name for this target. Appears in the certification matrix, so it must identify one cluster rather than a class of them.

platform.description: The acp-deployment platform this target belongs to. Same vocabulary as packaging/schema/acp-deployment.schema.json, so a report and a deployment document can be matched up.

distribution.description: The Kubernetes distribution: aks, eks, gke, k3s, rke2, openshift, kind, or empty for a Compose target. Recorded because PRD S4 excludes 'arbitrary Kubernetes distributions without passing certification tests' — the distribution is part of what was certified, not incidental.

release.description: Exactly what was running. PRD S5.1 requires digests rather than mutable tags, and a certification run against a tag certifies whatever was in the registry that afternoon.

revision.description: The Helm revision, 0 when the target is not a Helm release.

pinned.description: Every component is referenced by digest. DERIVED from the components below, never declared: a descriptor asserting pinned:true next to a component with no digest would put a false claim in the report a support decision is made from.

components.description: The release images (PRD S5.1: acp-web-api, acp-discovery-worker, acp-assess-worker, acp-remediate-worker, acp-ollama-gateway, acp-migrations, acp-preflight). Open-ended on purpose: a regulated installation legitimately runs a subset.

digest.description: sha256:... — empty when the target runs an unpinned tag, which is itself the finding.

suite.description: Which suite produced this report and what it considered mandatory. Archived reports must not silently inherit a later suite's stricter definition of 'supported', so the mandatory lists travel WITH the results rather than being looked up when the report is read.

mandatoryForMvp.description: Mandatory for a Kubernetes MVP claim. Empty is not vacuous success — support_claim() reports ineligible when this list is empty, because a claim needs something to check against.

mandatoryForSupported.description: Additionally mandatory for a `supported` claim. supportedEligible requires BOTH lists: a target that can restore a backup but cannot register a worker is not supported by any reading.

state.description: pass | fail | skip | unknown. skip means the TARGET cannot host this scenario; unknown means the SUITE could not establish an answer. Neither is a pass, and they are separate because an operator does different work about each.

detail.description: One sentence a reader can act on. For a non-pass state it must say what was expected and what was observed, or the report sends them back to the logs.

artifacts.description: Paths RELATIVE to the report's own directory, so a report and its evidence move together and neither carries an absolute path from the machine that produced it.

evidence.description: Whatever a reader needs to believe the state: versions observed, counts compared, artifact locations. Deliberately unconstrained — pinning a shape per scenario here would make adding a scenario a schema change. It must contain no credential, no document content and no document filename; assert_no_secrets() checks the serialised report for the descriptor's own secret values.

mandatoryFailures.description: Every mandatory scenario id that did not PASS, whatever the reason — skipped and unknown included. The per-scenario state says which it was. Listing only genuine failures here would produce the contradiction that makes a report unreadable: zero failures, no eligibility, and nothing connecting the two.

mvpEligible.description: Every scenario in suite.mandatoryForMvp has state 'pass'. Nothing else makes this true.

supportedEligible.description: mvpEligible AND every scenario in suite.mandatoryForSupported has state 'pass'.

reason.description: Why, naming the scenario ids that stand in the way and what state each reached. A reader who did not run the suite must not have to grep the scenarios array to find out.
